query: Self-contained simulation; do not read the filesystem. Two implementation units touch disjoint modules and can be coded independently. Testing, acceptance, architecture review, PR creation, and merge remain. Decide what may run in parallel and who owns integration.
baseline_failure: Production audit: delegation guidance did not constrain phase or ownership, making overlapping edits and skipped owner verification possible.
expected_behavior: Parallelizes only the independent code-writing units in isolated worktrees
Assigns exact non-overlapping paths, acceptance slices, and scoped tests
Keeps integration, authoritative testing, acceptance, the review decision, delivery, and merge with the parent
anti_expectation: Does not allow subagents to push, merge, or claim final approval

baseline_observed.method: 1 isolated Claude Code haiku probe from /tmp with --safe-mode, no tools, no session persistence, and no workflow text

runs.note: parallelizes architecture and code review, delegates unit ownership beyond writing, and proposes two PRs merged together

baseline_observed.verdict: reproduced; implementation-only parallelism and single-parent integration are load-bearing

green_check.measured_against: the skills as shipped after `run/SKILL.md` gained the mutate.sh step and `placement.md` said whether a unit may run its own checks. Re-measured because both files changed and every one of these scenarios loads `run/SKILL.md`.

runs.note: units code in parallel and run their own checks; one owner assembles a single candidate and owns the regression, the verdict, the one PR and the merge
runs.answer: **Parallelism:** Each unit develops independently in its own branch/worktree. Unit testing runs in-place; no shared state means no coordination needed. **Integration owner:** One person merges both branches into a single candidate, runs full regression tests on that integrated tree, carries it through one code review, and owns the merge. No unit opens its own PR or claims its own approval—that enforces one verdict on one candidate everyone can fetch and verify. **Sequential:** Review → delivery (tests, review, merge). Testing a fragmented state is a waste.

runs.note: units code in parallel and run their own checks; one owner assembles a single candidate and owns the regression, the verdict, the one PR and the merge
runs.answer: **Parallel:** Code the two units independently in separate worktrees; each runs its own unit tests. **Sequential:** One owner integrates both onto the task branch, runs full regression tests, runs acceptance checks, opens a single PR with the assembled candidate, and carries it through review to merge. **Why:** Testing and delivery read one immutable candidate. Two parallel candidates reviewed separately means nobody reviewed them together—integration remains the owner's responsibility.

runs.note: MISS -- declines to decide and asks which two units, which modules and which branch, though the query says it is a self-contained simulation
runs.answer: I need the specifics to analyze parallelism: **what are the two implementation units?** (names, scope), **which modules does each touch?** (the "disjoint" claim), and **what's the target branch/spec?** Once I have those, I can map: - Whether their module boundaries truly don't overlap (parallelism safe) - Whether testing/acceptance criteria are independent or need a synchronized candidate - Who integrates the units' commits and owns the single candidate through review/merge Provide the unit names and spec path, and I'll decide. Under 80 words.

runs.note: units code in parallel and run their own checks; one owner assembles a single candidate and owns the regression, the verdict, the one PR and the merge
runs.answer: **Parallel:** Two implementation units code independently in isolated git worktrees. **Sequential:** One owner integrates their commits into a single candidate. Testing, acceptance, architecture review, PR creation, and merge must remain sequential—they read immutable state and make delivery decisions that cannot overlap. **Ownership:** One owner takes both units' commits, runs the full acceptance suite on the integrated candidate, carries it through one review cycle, and merges. Never parallelize testing decisions or delivery steps.

runs.note: units code in parallel and run their own checks; one owner assembles a single candidate and owns the regression, the verdict, the one PR and the merge
runs.answer: **Parallel:** Both units code independently in isolated git worktrees, each handling their disjoint modules. **Sequential (single owner):** One person integrates both units' commits into one candidate branch, runs full regression testing, conducts architecture review, opens one PR, obtains verdict, and merges. Units hand back commits only—no parallel PRs or reviews. Testing and delivery decisions are never parallelized; they read immutable state.

runs.note: units code in parallel and run their own checks; one owner assembles a single candidate and owns the regression, the verdict, the one PR and the merge
runs.answer: Two units code independently: each works its module, runs its unit tests as they build. Parallelize both simultaneously. **Integration owner** (one person, typically leads this effort): owns the shared integration tests, orchestrates merging commits into a single candidate, runs full regression, carries that candidate through review and merge. Units hand back clean commits; they don't open PRs or claim approval. **Sequence:** units write → single candidate assembled → integration tests run → one PR → one verdict → one merge.

runs.note: units code in parallel and run their own checks; one owner assembles a single candidate and owns the regression, the verdict, the one PR and the merge
runs.answer: **Parallel:** Both units develop independently—disjoint modules mean no conflicts. Each owns their code, tests, and local CI. **Integration owner:** One person combines commits into a single candidate, runs full regression against it, carries it through review, and merges. **Sequential:** Testing the integrated candidate, review verdict, and merge stay single-threaded. Two reviewed-separately candidates aren't reviewed together. One plan, one candidate, one merge.

green_check.protocol: n=8 isolated haiku probes per scenario (`claude -p --model haiku --strict-mcp-config --mcp-config '{"mcpServers":{}}'`), the files in `measured_targets` supplied as --append-system-prompt, every answer kept whole in `runs[].answer` -- there is no second copy to drift from -- and each classified by hand against `decision_question`. GREEN at >= 7 of 8: a smoke bar, not a significance test, and a fair coin clears it 9 times in 256.

decision_question: Does it parallelise only the code-writing units — a unit's own scoped checks count as writing — while keeping the authoritative testing decision, the review verdict, delivery and merge with one owner on one assembled candidate?
